The title suggests a disconnect between movement rhetoric and perceived local outcomes. The article appears to examine public opinion within a specific political-health constituency. It offers a snapshot of how health messaging is landing in rural America.

articles.title: STAT Plus: At MAHA Summit, a grassroots movement goes corporate
articles.summary_4_sentences: This article reports that the MAHA movement's summit showed a grassroots effort becoming more corporate. The title suggests corporate interests are overshadowing the movement's original base. That shift may affect credibility, priorities and public perception. The piece examines the commercialization of a health-adjacent political movement.

articles.title: STAT Plus: How a young doctor rose from rural New Mexico to FDA commissioner nominee
articles.summary_4_sentences: This profile traces how a young doctor from rural New Mexico became an FDA commissioner nominee. The article appears to focus on Heidi Overton's background and rise. Leadership profiles can offer context for how nominees may approach agency priorities. The piece provides biographical framing around a consequential regulatory appointment.

articles.title: FDA nominee Overton parries vaccine questions at Senate hearing
articles.summary_4_sentences: At a Senate hearing, FDA commissioner nominee Heidi Overton fielded questions on vaccines and other contentious issues. The summary says she pledged to follow the law on key decisions and work to speed early drug research. The hearing offered lawmakers a chance to probe how she might handle politically sensitive topics. The article captures the confirmation-stage scrutiny facing a potential FDA leader.

articles.title: AI will inflate healthcare costs before lowering them, Oz says
articles.summary_4_sentences: CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz said AI will raise healthcare costs before it lowers them. He warned that AI could turbocharge medical billing in the short term, even if long-term savings eventually emerge. The comment reflects concern that automation may first amplify existing incentives in the payment system. The article adds a prominent policymaker's view to the debate over AI's economic impact on care.
